subject.title: MEDIA: directive with absolute local paths outside default media roots silently fails (Telegram)

question: Should this issue be scoped to blocked-media diagnostics while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/47002 owns configurable root expansion, or should this issue change the host-local media root policy itself?
rationale: The local diagnostics fix is narrow, but accepting more absolute host paths changes a security-sensitive file-read/upload boundary and overlaps with the broader root-policy design.

options.title: Diagnostics here, root policy elsewhere
options.body: Keep this issue focused on clearer Telegram/media failure feedback and let https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/47002 or the approved filesystem-roots design own persistent root expansion.

options.title: Define root expansion here
options.body: Use this issue as the canonical place to specify and implement a supported configurable media root contract for `MEDIA:` replies.

options.title: Close as documented boundary
options.body: Treat blocked out-of-policy paths as working as designed and rely on managed roots, `tools.fs` policy, or the message tool instead.

recommendation.title: Diagnostics here, root policy elsewhere
recommendation.body: Keep this issue focused on clearer Telegram/media failure feedback and let https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/47002 or the approved filesystem-roots design own persistent root expansion.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent source-history connection to outbound media access policy and the host-local media boundary.
